answer: Bonded collateral makes each identity costly to operate, while evidence linking coordinated equivocation lets the protocol aggregate responsibility rather than treat aliases independently. For k identities, correlated violations incur penalties proportional to k², so a swarm’s loss rises faster than its size; detection can also trigger an exponential multiplier on forfeited capital. If nadir, jade, and delta are three aliases acting together, splitting votes among them does not dilute the shared liability.
